definition: Infinite limits and limits at infinity distinguish local unbounded behavior from long-run behavior. Vertical asymptotes arise near finite inputs; horizontal or slant behavior describes what happens as the input magnitude grows.

Continuity at an input requires an existing function value, an existing limit, and agreement between them. Continuity on an interval supports global conclusions such as the Intermediate Value Theorem.

A limit describes the output behavior produced by inputs approaching a target. The value at the target may agree with the limit, differ from it, or be undefined. Numerical, graphical, and algebraic evidence should be reconciled.
